query: How does resolution time vary across issue themes, channel, and priority?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Directly provides the 'issue themes' axis the query asks for. Categorizations are well-grounded (billing duplicate line item -> billing_issue, session drops -> auth_access, feature enhancement -> feature_request). CS-0003 502 outage labeled performance_degradation is a defensible reading though 'integration/outage' might fit better; still sound.

per_column.name: blocker_status
per_column.rationale: A blocking/urgency axis adds leverage beyond raw priority and can correlate with resolution time. Some values are inferential: CS-0001 (wants corrected invoice before Friday) marked True is a stretch, and CS-0005 (added manual workaround) marked True is arguable since a workaround exists. Reasonable but occasionally over-asserts blocking where text is softer.

per_column.name: affected_user_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact is a genuine new grouping axis plausibly linked to resolution time. Values mostly grounded (all Acme tenant members -> entire_tenant; single customer invoice -> single_user). CS-0004 'power users'/'multiple_users' is inferred from 'power users' phrasing—reasonable but the text does not clearly state multiple affected users.

per_column.name: issue_type_specificity
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes bug/outage/config/feature types, a useful modeling axis partly distinct from issue_category. Mostly grounded, but CS-0001 labeled account_admin_action fits (needs corrected invoice issued), and CS-0002 session-drop labeled reproducible_bug conflicts somewhat with the customer's own SSO-config suspicion; borderline but defensible.

per_column.name: cross_system_dependency
per_column.rationale: A dependency flag is a reasonable axis for resolution-time analysis. However CS-0002 (customer suspects SSO config push from their IT/external system) marked False, and CS-0003 (gateway/infrastructure) marked False look inconsistent, while CS-0005 (Snowflake pipeline) correctly True. Some values contradict the evident external dependency in the text.

per_column.name: actionability
per_column.rationale: Who must act is analytically valuable and relates to resolution time. But grounding is uneven: CS-0002 marked customer_config_change though the customer wants confirmation from support, and CS-0004 (feature request needing eng) marked internal_eng_fix_required is fine, whereas CS-0001 billing correction as support_escalation is defensible. Several assignments are speculative given silent text.

judge.rationale: The added columns give multiple genuine grouping axes (theme, scope, blocker, type, dependency, actionability) that directly serve a query about how resolution time varies by theme/channel/priority; none are near-constant or trivial restatements. Groundedness is generally good for extractive categorizations (issue_category, affected_user_scope) but weaker for inferential flags—cross_system_dependency and actionability show some values that conflict with or over-assert beyond the source text.
